title: Bounded cohomology in a weak Serre class is thick
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] and let $D(\mathcal A)$ be its ordinary unbounded derived category, with cohomology functors $H^n$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal B$ be a strictly full subcategory of $\mathcal A$ containing zero, closed under kernels and cokernels in $\mathcal A$ of morphisms between its objects, and closed under extensions: in any short exact sequence $0\to B_1\to M\to B_2\to0$ with $B_1,B_2\in\mathcal B$, also $M\in\mathcal B$. Let $D^b_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal A)$ consist of those $K$ for which every $H^n(K)$ belongs to $\mathcal B$ and $H^n(K)=0$ outside some finite integer interval. Then $D^b_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal A)$ is thick in $D(\mathcal A)$ [pur9-def-thick]: it contains zero and is closed under isomorphisms, shifts, distinguished triangles, and all ambient retracts. More precisely, if $L\xrightarrow{i}K\xrightarrow{r}L$ has $ri=1_L$ and $K\in D^b_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal A)$, then $H^n(i)$ identifies $H^n(L)$ with $\ker(1-H^n(i)H^n(r))$ in $\mathcal A$, and any cohomological interval bound for $K$ is also a bound for $L$.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal S=D^b_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal A)$. By [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], membership in $D^b(\mathcal A)$ means that only finitely many $H^n$ are nonzero. A finite subset of $\mathbf Z$ is contained in an integer interval (use $[0,0]$ for the empty subset). Thus $\mathcal S=D_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal A)\cap D^b(\mathcal A)$, with $D_{\mathcal B}$ the full subcategory defined by the cohomology condition alone.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-cohomology-in-weak-serre-subcategory] to the given $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$: its hypotheses are precisely strict fullness, zero, kernels and cokernels between objects of $\mathcal B$, and extensions, all assumed here. Its bounded-intersection clause makes $\mathcal S$ a full triangulated subcategory with the inherited shifts and triangles. The unbounded cohomology-condition category is strictly full by that same statement, and $D^b(\mathcal A)$ is strictly full by [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], so their intersection is strictly full. Consequently $\mathcal S$ contains zero and is closed under isomorphisms, all integer shifts, and two-out-of-three in distinguished triangles (rotate a triangle to put the unknown vertex in the middle, using shift closure); the inherited triangulated structure is that of [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory].

source.place: Tag 06UQ, lemma-cohomology-in-serre-subcategory, including bounded versions; explicit kernel-universal-property expansion of its direct-summand argument.

proof.text: For an arbitrary ambient retract $L\xrightarrow{i}K\xrightarrow{r}L$, $ri=1_L$, fix $n$ and write $N=H^n(L)$, $M=H^n(K)$, $I=H^n(i)$ and $R=H^n(r)$. Functoriality in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives $RI=1_N$. Work in the abelian category [def-sp-abelian], whose bilinear composition and subtraction are as in [def-weil-preadditive-category]. Set $q=1_M-IR$. Then $qI=I-I(RI)=0$. For any object $T$ and morphism $u:T\to M$ with $qu=0$, one has $u=IRu=I(Ru)$; this factorization through $I$ is unique because $Iv=u$ implies $v=RIv=Ru$. This is exactly the kernel universal property, so $I$ identifies $N$ with $\ker(1_M-IR)$.

source.place: Tag 06UQ, lemma-cohomology-in-serre-subcategory, including bounded versions; explicit kernel-universal-property expansion of its direct-summand argument.

proof.text: If $K\in\mathcal S$, then $M=H^n(K)\in\mathcal B$. The map $q$ in the preceding step is an endomorphism of $M$; since $\mathcal B$ is full, it is a morphism between objects of $\mathcal B$. The assumed kernel closure puts $\ker q$ in $\mathcal B$, and strict fullness together with the displayed kernel identification puts $H^n(L)$ in $\mathcal B$. If $H^n(K)=0$, both $I:N\to M$ and $R:M\to N$ factor through zero, hence $1_N=RI=0$. In an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] this makes $N$ a zero object: every map into or out of $N$ equals its composition with $1_N=0$ and so is the unique zero map. Thus any interval $[a,b]$ outside which the cohomology of $K$ vanishes also bounds that of $L$. This proves $L\in\mathcal S$ for every ambient retract and proves the sharper bound assertion.

source.place: Tag 06UQ, lemma-cohomology-in-serre-subcategory, including bounded versions; explicit kernel-universal-property expansion of its direct-summand argument.

proof.text: Step 2 gives zero, isomorphism, shift and triangle closure, and steps 3-4 give all ambient retracts, in particular direct summands. These are the conditions of [pur9-def-thick], so $D^b_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal A)$ is thick. Step 3 is the asserted cohomological kernel formula, and step 4 shows that the same interval bound works for every retract.
